title: Atom Probe Analysis for Hydrogen Catalyst Materials
content: Hydrogen is one of the potential candidates for sustainable energy sources with high energy density. Although hydrogen is environmentally harmless, there remain challenges to produce hydrogen with cost efficiency. Therefore, catalytic materials are required for producing hydrogen to enhance the reaction efficiency with high activity, selectivity, and stability, such as iridium-based materials and platinum-based materials. The mechanism for hydrogen production of these catalytic materials is commonly considered to be an adsorption and desorption of protons on the surface of these catalytic materials during the catalytic reactions, including HER (Hydrogen Evolution Reaction) and HOR (Hydrogen Oxidation Reaction). However, little is reported and observed about the actual behavior of hydrogen during catalytic reactions. Atom probe tomography is one of the powerful instruments for detecting and analyzing hydrogen in various materials, with high reliability when utilizing deuterium for the hydrogen signal source. Herein, we utilize atom probe tomography (APT) and introduce deuterium charging workflow for comprehensive and atomic-scale analysis for hydrogen catalysts such as iridium and platinum.
